answer.sql: WITH target_measures AS (SELECT UNNEST(CAST(ARRAY['READM_30_PN', 'MORT_30_HF', 'SEP_1'] AS TEXT[])) AS measure_id), national_latest AS (SELECT UPPER(mv.measure_id) AS measure_id, mv.score, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY mv.facility_id, UPPER(mv.measure_id) ORDER BY mv.period_end DESC NULLS LAST) AS rn FROM hq.measure_values AS mv JOIN hq.hospitals AS h ON h.facility_id = mv.facility_id JOIN target_measures AS tm ON UPPER(tm.measure_id) = UPPER(mv.measure_id) WHERE mv.score IS NOT NULL), national_averages AS (SELECT measure_id, AVG(score) AS national_avg FROM national_latest WHERE rn = 1 GROUP BY measure_id), national_avg_pivot AS (SELECT MAX(national_avg) FILTER(WHERE measure_id = 'READM_30_PN') AS readm_avg, MAX(national_avg) FILTER(WHERE measure_id = 'MORT_30_HF') AS mort_avg, MAX(national_avg) FILTER(WHERE measure_id = 'SEP_1') AS sepsis_avg FROM national_averages), houston_scores AS (SELECT facility_id, facility_name, MAX(score) FILTER(WHERE UPPER(measure_id) = 'READM_30_PN') AS readm_rate, MAX(score) FILTER(WHERE UPPER(measure_id) = 'MORT_30_HF') AS mort_rate, MAX(score) FILTER(WHERE UPPER(measure_id) = 'SEP_1') AS sepsis_pct FROM hq.v_tx_latest WHERE is_houston_area IS TRUE AND UPPER(county) IN ('HARRIS', 'FORT BEND', 'MONTGOMERY', 'GALVESTON', 'BRAZORIA') AND UPPER(measure_id) IN ('READM_30_PN', 'MORT_30_HF', 'SEP_1') GROUP BY facility_id, facility_name) SELECT hs.facility_name AS hospital, hs.readm_rate AS pneumonia_30_day_readmission_rate, hs.mort_rate AS heart_failure_30_day_death_rate, hs.sepsis_pct AS sepsis_care_percentage FROM houston_scores AS hs CROSS JOIN national_avg_pivot AS na WHERE hs.readm_rate < na.readm_avg AND hs.mort_rate < na.mort_avg AND hs.sepsis_pct > na.sepsis_avg ORDER BY hs.readm_rate ASC, hs.facility_name ASC LIMIT 200

answer.answer: Timely and effective care measures show the share of patients receiving treatments associated with the best results for certain common, serious conditions or procedures, how quickly hospitals treat certain medical emergencies, and how well they provide preventive services. records.question: What changed when Medicare Advantage admissions were added to the hospital-wide readmission measure?

answer.question: What changed when Medicare Advantage admissions were added to the hospital-wide readmission measure?
answer.answer: The only measure change was adding Medicare Advantage admissions to the cohort; the other specifications stayed the same. In the tested period, this added more than four million admissions and 127 hospitals, including 63 additional hospitals meeting the 25-admission reporting cutoff. The combined FFS-and-MA cohort had a slightly higher mean risk-standardized readmission rate than the FFS-only cohort (15.48% versus 15.35%) and higher test-retest reliability (0.780 versus 0.725). About 67% of hospitals stayed in the same performance quintile, and 95% stayed within one quintile; the report says the addition improved reliability and score precision and included more hospitals and beneficiaries.

records.question: Which interventions make up the SEP-1 numerator, and which patients are excluded?

answer.question: Which interventions make up the SEP-1 numerator, and which patients are excluded?
answer.answer: The numerator includes denominator patients who receive all applicable interventions: initial lactate measurement, blood cultures, antibiotics, fluid resuscitation, repeat lactate measurement, vasopressors, and reassessment of volume status and tissue perfusion. For severe sepsis, initial lactate, blood cultures before antibiotics, and antibiotics are due within 3 hours; repeat lactate is due within 6 hours if the initial level is above 2 mmol/L. For septic shock, 30 ml/kg crystalloid is due within 3 hours for hypotension or lactate = 4 mmol/L; within 6 hours, vasopressors are used for hypotension not responding to initial fluids, and reassessment is required for persistent hypotension (MAP < 65 mm Hg) after fluids or initial lactate = 4 mmol/L. Exclusions are patients without severe sepsis; those transferred from another acute-care facility; those receiving IV antibiotics for more than 24 hours before severe-sepsis presentation; those with comfort or palliative-care directives within 3 hours of severe-sepsis presentation or within 6 hours of septic-shock presentation; those with an administrative contraindication to care within 6 hours of presentation of severe sepsis or septic shock; patients with septic shock or severe sepsis discharged within 6 hours of presentation; patients with a stay longer than 120 days; and patients included in a clinical trial.
